title: From States to Dynamics: Detecting Rule Violations in OthelloGPT
abstract: arXiv:2611.29715v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sequence models trained on game moves have been shown to encode world models, with structured linear probes revealing the underlying game states. World models, however, are inherently dynamic: in deterministic board games, a set of rules constrain how states evolve over time. We therefore ask if and how OthelloGPT, a transformer trained only on Othello move sequences, manifests the rules of the game in its activation space. We divide the rules of Othello, and symmetrically their violations, into three classes: placing a disc on an empty square (R1), flanking an opponent's disc (R2), and moving in turn (R3). We find that linear probes accurately separate legal from illegal moves, and also distinguish between the three kinds of rule violations. We introduce an unsupervised rule-violation detector based on the step length of activations between consecutive moves, which identifies illegal moves above chance. We further improve our detection

translated_title: 从状态到动态：检测OthelloGPT中的规则违规
translated_abstract: 训练于游戏走子序列的序列模型已被证明能够编码世界模型，结构化的线性探针可以揭示其潜在的博弈状态。然而，世界模型本质上是动态的：在确定性棋盘游戏中，一组规则约束着状态如何随时间演化。因此，我们提出这样的问题：OthelloGPT——一个仅在黑白棋（Othello）走子序列上训练的transformer——是否以及如何在其激活空间中体现游戏的规则。我们将黑白棋的规则（以及对称地，相应的违规行为）分为三类：在空格上放置棋子（R1）、夹住对方棋子（R2）、按顺序轮流走子（R3）。我们发现线性探针能够准确区分合法与非法走子，并且还能区分这三种不同类型的规则违规。我们引入了一种基于连续走子之间激活步长的无监督规则违规检测器，它能够以高于随机水平的准确率识别非法走子。我们进一步改进了我们的检测方法……
tldr: 该论文研究了OthelloGPT在激活空间中如何体现黑白棋的动态规则，将规则违规分为三类并证明线性探针可以区分它们，同时提出了一种基于激活步长的无监督规则违规检测方法。
en_tdlr: This paper investigates how OthelloGPT, a transformer trained only on Othello move sequences, manifests game rules in its activation space, showing that linear probes can distinguish three classes of rule violations and introducing an unsupervised rule-violation detector based on activation step lengths between consecutive moves.
